BARRIER LAW.notes: Note : All 'Wall' spells on this list (except Wall of Force and Shadow Wall ) require that at least 1 cubic root of the material of which the wall consists be within 50' of the caster. Wall material will generally match that of 'model' material (e.g., if the local rock is limestone, a Wall of Stone will also be limestone). See Spell Law Section 10.20 for additional details on Wall spells.

CONCUSSION'S WAY.notes: Note : See Spell Law Section 10.9 for the application of wound-healing spells (various Relief , Healing , and Healing True spells). While medical treatment of the wound is miraculously immediate, the body will still need a period of recovery before the injury has healed, depending on several factors, including which type of wound-healing spell is used.

DETECTION MASTERY.notes: Note : See Spell Law Section 10.4 for more about detection spells.

LIGHT'S WAY.notes: Note : None of the 'Aura' spells ( Aura , True Aura , Mass Aura , Mass True Aura and Alkar ) are cumulative with each other or Blur . The Gamemaster may wish to allow the bonus from these spells to apply to Leadership as well as defense. Consult Core Law Section 15.7 for dealing with light and darkness.

LOFTY MOVEMENTS.notes: Note : Spells that involve teleportation are normally quite noisy and difficult to silence. Air is being pushed about in a manner not unlike a thunderclap. Amount of noise depends on the size of the object teleported.

NATURE'S LAW.notes:
Note : An herb is defined as a plant that, in its raw form or when specially prepared, provides some unusual benefit to the user. This does not apply to poisons, but may apply to narcotics.

See Spell Law Section 10.17 for additional details about Lore spells.

PURIFICATIONS.notes:
Note : In no case do these spells allow the disease or poison removed to make an RR.

Parasitic infestation is considered a disease for purposes of this list.

SOUND'S WAY.notes: Note : See Spell Law Section 10.17 for details on using elemental spells, like Silence and Quiet , on living targets.

SPELL DEFENSE.notes:
Note : A Hybrid spell will be affected by a Cancel , Dispel , or Shield spell that is effective against either of its hybridized realms.

Curses are not affected by regular dispelling. See Spell Law Section 10.2 for dealing with curses.

WEATHER WAYS.notes:
Note : All weather generating spells cause weather to gradually form over a period of one minute. In addition, weather generating spells have no effect in areas where there are not normally occurring weather patterns (i.e., inside buildings, etc.).

Weather Prediction is based on current conditions. Natural evolution of the weather system produces some uncertainty, which is represented by the 5% chance of error. Magical or divine intervention can alter weather patterns beyond those natural uncertainty parameters and completely void the Weather Prediction (e.g., a 'sunny and clear' prediction is made for the next three days. Later that day, another caster casts a Storm Call in the area. That disturbs local weather patterns and the Weather Prediction must be recast in order to learn what the new weather pattern is likely to produce).

BLOOD LAW.notes:
Note : A flesh wound is also classified as a 'skin & tissue injury'. Injury penalties from cuts (i.e., wounds that also caused bleeding) are likewise flesh wounds and 'skin & tissue injuries,' and are treated with Flesh Relief or Flesh Healing spells. See Core Law Section 13.1 .

See Spell Law Section 10.9 for the application of wound-healing spells (various Relief , Healing , and Healing True spells). While medical treatment of the wound is miraculously immediate, the body will still need a period of recovery before the injury has healed, depending on several factors, including which type of wound-healing spell is used.

BONE LAW.notes: Note : See Spell Law Section 10.9 for the application of wound-healing spells (various Relief , Healing , and Healing True spells). While medical treatment of the wound is miraculously immediate, the body will still need a period of recovery before the injury has healed, depending on several factors, including which type of wound-healing spell is used.

CALM SPIRITS.notes:
Note : An 'aggressive' action is defined as any action with the intent to directly harm any individual(s). Actions that result in harm indirectly to individuals are not 'aggressive'. Pulling the lever on the wall to drop an individual into a pit is an aggressive action (the action directly resulted in the harm). Running away to get help is not an aggressive action.

See Spell Law Section 10.21 for a discussion of spells with 'Kind' in their name.

CREATIONS.notes: Note : All nutritional spells on this list miraculously adapt to the consumer. Food Production might feed a mouse or an elephant as easily as a man. Results of attempts to subvert this spell by creating food for a dragon then feeding it to humans should reflect the nature of the deity called on.

LOCATING WAYS.notes: Note : See Spell Law Section 10.16 for information on interpretation of 'path'.

LORE.notes:
Note : This list may be learned by 'Evil' Channeling users as 'Dark Lore', in which case just reverse the 'Light'/'Dark' and 'White'/'Black' Lore spells. (E.g., if one learns the Dark Lore list, the 17th level spell is Dark Lore III and works on 'unholy' rather than 'holy' items.)

See Spell Law Section 10.4 for more about detection spells.

MUSCLE LAW.notes: Note : See Spell Law Section 10.9 for the application of wound-healing spells (various Relief , Healing , and Healing True spells). While medical treatment of the wound is miraculously immediate, the body will still need a period of recovery before the injury has healed, depending on several factors, including which type of wound-healing spell is used.

NERVE & ORGAN LAW.notes: Note : See Spell Law Section 10.9 for the application of wound-healing spells (various Relief , Healing , and Healing True spells). While medical treatment of the wound is miraculously immediate, the body will still need a period of recovery before the injury has healed, depending on several factors, including which type of wound-healing spell is used.

SYMBOLIC WAYS.notes:
Note : A symbol is permanent unless destroyed by Unsymbol or the stone it is placed upon is moved. Symbols are not affected by Dispel spells.

The precise size of a Symbol may vary. Suggested sizes range from 3'x3' to 1'x1'.

For spells with a duration of Concentration, treat it as 1 round/level when cast by a Symbol.

If a spell list skill bonus is used in the resolution of a spell, use the bonus for a number of ranks equal to the level of the spell (e.g., the bonus for a 7th level spell would be +35).

When a spell from a Symbol requires an RR, assume an SCR of 50.

CHANNELS.notes:
Note : For the Sanctuary and Sanctuary's Return spells, normal encumbrance rules apply (see Spell Law Section 10.15 ).

Note that the spells on this list may vary in appearance or usage based upon the nature of the deity the caster serves. GMs should feel free to replace some of the spells above for spells more appropriate to the deity. For example, a god(dess) of fire might have several spells replaced with spells adapted from the Magician's Fire Law list.

The GM should be careful and clear when defining 'alignment' for the Holy Shout spell. Targets should include all folk who are not specifically following the caster's religion (and thus it might include some allies). Depending on the state of theology in game world, this might mean that to avoid the effects one needs to worship the caster's deity, or it might merely require that a deity of the same mythos be followed (e.g., in a world using Greek, Norse, Indian, Chinese, and Celtic gods, a devotee of Zeus might be considered of the same 'alignment' as a priest of Poseidon).

COMMUNAL WAYS.notes: Note: See Spell Law Section 10.5 for more on dreams and symbology in divination.

LIFE MASTERY.notes:
Note : 'Life' is assumed to be life on the caster's world. Aliens or creatures from other planes of existence do not count as life for the purposes of these spells.

See Spell Law Section 10.12 for information on Life, Lifegiving, and Life Drain.

PROTECTIONS.notes: Note : Resistance , Prayer , Bless , and Protective Spheres are not cumulative with each other for a single effect, but may be combined to include more effects. E.g., someone who had been the single target of Bless III and then received Prayer I would get +15 DB and +15 maneuver rolls. The Prayer would not increase the maneuver roll bonus, but would provide a +5 to RRs.

REPULSIONS.notes:
Note : See Creature Law for more information about the undead. The GM may wish to give RR modifications for certain very powerful undead. Also, GMs may wish to modify the undead-affecting spells to be more/less powerful when on holy/unholy ground (see Treasure Law ).

A Hybrid spell will be affected by a Cancel or Dispel spell that is effective against either of its hybridized realms.

See Spell Law Section 10.2 for more on curses and removing them.

SUMMONS.notes:
Note : If the creature can understand the caster (e.g. Animal Tongues ), the creature can be controlled through normal communication. Otherwise, control is maintained only through the concentration of the caster.

Spells that involve teleportation are normally quite noisy and difficult to silence. Air is being pushed about in a manner not unlike a thunderclap. Amount of noise depends on the size of the object teleported.

When allowed to choose more than one option on summoning spells, the same option may be chosen more than once. For example, with a Summons III , two options are available. This means that if both options are used for the same thing, then three first-level creatures could be summoned, or one third-level creature could be summoned, or one first-level creature could be summoned for four times as long.

Demons are assumed to be hostile beings of another plane who are brought into the caster's plane through the use of an elemental force (one not of the demon's plane). Thus, the demon and caster do not make RRs during the summons. See Creature Law for information on specific demons. While written with Evil spell lists in mind, Spell Law Section 10.3 may also be useful.

While Summons spells on this list are of type 'U', the creatures summoned are automatically considered willing to serve as described.

ANIMAL MASTERY.notes:
Note : When allowed to choose more than one option on summoning spells, the same option may be chosen more than once. For example, with an Animal Summons III , two options are available. This means that if both options are used for the same thing, then three first-level creatures could be summoned, one third-level creature could be summoned, or one first-level creature could be summoned for four times as long.

See Creature Law for more information on animals. For purposes of this list consider anything in the 'Animals' chapter of Creature Law , and nothing outside that chapter, to be an animal.

While Summons spells on this list are of type 'U', the creatures summoned are automatically considered willing to serve as described.

HERB MASTERY.notes: Note : See Treasure Law Section 2.3 for details on herbs.

NATURE'S LORE.notes: Note : Weather Prediction is based on current conditions. Natural evolution of the weather system produces some uncertainty, which is represented by the 5% chance of error. Magical or divine intervention can alter weather patterns beyond those natural uncertainty parameters and completely void the Weather Prediction (e.g., a 'sunny and clear' prediction is made for the next three days. Later that day, another caster casts a Storm Call in the area. That disturbs local weather patterns and the Weather Prediction must be recast in order to learn what the new weather pattern is likely to produce).

NATURE'S PROTECTION.notes:
Note : Hues and Shadow are obviously incompatible.

Illusions (which include the Façade spells) are one of the more complex and subtle types of magic and they are explained at length in Spell Law Section 10.10 .

NATURE'S WRATH.notes:
Note : Nature's Ire and Nature's Might spells are negated if the caster sleeps.

If Nature's Might and Nature's Ire True are combined, the concussion hit damage done is triple normal.

See Spell Law Section 10.2 regarding curses.

PLANT MASTERY.notes: Note : Spells from this list may be applied to fungi with a Hard Spell Mastery maneuver.

CURSEBREAKING.notes:
Note : A Hybrid spell will be affected by a Cancel , Holy Cancellation , or Dispel spell that is effective against either of its hybridized realms.

Curses are not affected by regular dispelling. See Spell Law Section 10.2 for dealing with curses.

HOLY HEALING.notes:
Note : The wound healing spells on this list will treat all types of wounds except nerve and brain damage.

See Spell Law Section 10.9 for the application of wound-healing spells (various Relief , Healing , and Healing True spells). While medical treatment of the wound is miraculously immediate, the body will still need a period of recovery before the injury has healed, depending on several factors, including which type of wound-healing spell is used.

HOLY SHIELDS.notes:
Note : None of the 'Aura' spells ( Aura , True Aura , Mass Aura , and Alkar ) are cumulative with each other or Blur. The Gamemaster may wish to allow the bonus from these spells to apply to Leadership as well as defense.

When under the effects of an Unpain spell, there are no penalties for hits lost. Full effects of the lost hits occur when the spell duration ends. However, if the hits are healed before the duration ends, there is no effect. So, a character could be reduced to -38 hits while sustained by Unpain , but restored to 2 hits before the duration of the spell ended. He would never pass out. Likewise, if Unpain allows fighting beyond lethal hit loss, this has no effect until the spell expires.

The GM should be careful and clear when defining 'alignment'. Depending on the state of theology in the game world, this might mean that one needs to worship the caster's deity, or it might merely require that a deity of the same mythos be followed (e.g., in a world using Greek, Norse, Indian, Chinese, and Celtic gods, a devotee of Zeus might be considered of the same 'alignment' as a priest of Poseidon).

HOLY WAR.notes:
Note : Smite spell criticals do not get adjusted by size.

An 'enemy' for purposes of this list is not just someone the caster is fighting against at the moment. It must be someone (or something) who bears a conscious and lasting hostility to the caster's religion.

INSPIRING WAYS.notes:
Note : Voice and Words spells will only work on targets who are not actively hostile to the caster.

Voice and Words spells increase favorable reactions. This effect lasts 1 hour per level of the caster after the caster stops speaking. After this duration, the target's natural tendencies and reactions will take over. Note that most targets will continue to believe the caster even after the spell has lapsed.

Any target who resists a Voice or Words spell by more than 50 will realize that the caster was using magical influence.

BEASTLY WAYS.notes: Note : With the exceptions of Lion Claws and Shark Bite , the caster does not physically change with any of the spells on this list.

INNER WALLS.notes: Note: See Spell Law Section 10.2 for more about curses.

NATURE'S GUISES.notes:
Note : Hues and Shadow are obviously incompatible, but either might be combined with Shade .

Illusions (which include the Façade spells) are one of the more complex and subtle types of magic and they are explained at length in Spell Law Section 10.10 .

PATHMASTERY.notes: Note : See Spell Law Section 10.16 for information on interpretation of 'path'.

DARK CHANNELS.notes:
Note : See Spell Law Section 10.8 for guidelines for handling 'good' and 'evil'.

Absolution does not kill the body, so Dark Absolution leaves a living, but soulless body.

DEMONIC PACTS.notes:
Note : The desires of demons vary just as those of mortals do, but they generally desire freedom upon the mortal plane, blood, and material goods of significant value. Their price for aid varies depending on what is asked, the kind and individual personality of the demon, and other factors. A foolish bargain can rebound on the caster. Some demons deal in 'souls', but as such can only be offered once, one should haggle most carefully before making that trade.

A demon can only be affected by one Unleash Demon spell during any one stay on a given plane.

See more about dealing with summoned demons in Spell Law Section 10.3 .

Because of the extremely strong and intimate bond created between cast er and familiar, any attempt to dispel this bond suffers a penalty of 100 (normally a +100 bonus to the bond's RR against the dispelling attempt).

DEMONIC SUMMONS.notes:
Note : Statements about how long the demon can remain on this plane are based on the demon having arrived by means of a Summon Demon spell. If the demon arrived by some other means, it may well be able to stay longer.

See Creature Law for much more on demons and Spell Law Section 10.3 for more on demon summoning.

DISEASE.notes:
Note : It is an Easy maneuver with an appropriate medical skill to recognize any of these afflictions as the result of magic rather than natural disease.

When selecting allergies, the caster cannot choose something that the target is in constant contact with. For example, the caster cannot choose for the target to be allergic to himself, air, dirt, etc.

Once caught, diseases cannot be dispelled with Dispelling spells. How ever, they can be cured by Undisease or Remove Disease spells.

Unless stated otherwise, the diseases gained through this list are not contagious.

Unless stated otherwise, disease effects kick in d10 hours after the spell is cast.

WOUNDING.notes:
Note : All spells on this list have a range of 2'. In melee, it is presumed that you are within 2' of your opponent every round.

See Spell Law Section 10.12 for notes on Life Draining.

DETECTING WAYS.notes:
Note : Detect 'Realm' spells will detect hybrid magic including the realm in question.

See Spell Law Section 10.4 for more about detection spells.

ELEMENTAL SHIELDS.notes:
Note : Spells on this list are not cumulative.

Sphere spells on this list may be placed on a willing target and will move with them.

ESSENCE'S PERCEPTIONS.notes: Note : The 'Presence' ability detects minds of better than animal intelligence (i.e., creatures with the 'Animalistic' or 'Mindless' flaws are not detected). The caster will be aware of proximity to within 10' distance, and a 1 AP action will provide general direction (above, below, left, right, before, or behind) to one mind. If a detected mind belongs to a seen and recognized (as intelligent) being, then the caster will be able to identify the detected mind as belonging to that being.

LESSER ILLUSIONS.notes:
Note : If more that one option can be added to the Illusion or Phantasms spell, the same option can be chosen more than once. For Example - with an Illusion III , two options are available. The range could be doubled once to 200' and then doubled again to 400'.

Illusions are one of the more complex and subtle types of magic and they are explained at length in Spell Law Section 10.10 .

PHYSICAL ENHANCEMENT.notes: Note : See Core Law Section 15.7 for more on vision in low light and darkness.

RUNE MASTERY.notes:
Note : Rune Paper is a special prepared paper, designed to hold enchantments. After the rune is read from the paper, it fades from the paper. The paper may then hold another rune.

See Spell Law Section 4.7 for the use of runes.

SPELL WALL.notes: Note : A Hybrid spell will be affected by a Cancel , Dispel , or Shield spell that is effective against either of its hybridized realms.

UNBARRING WAYS.notes: Note : See Spell Law Section 10.14 regarding the use of spells from this list on varying qualities of locks and traps.

DISPELLING WAYS.notes:
Note : A Hybrid spell will be affected by a Cancel , Dispel , or Shield spell that is effective against either of its hybridized realms. Unessence , Unmentalism , and Unchanneling remove half the PP of a Hybrid using the applicable realm, but do not prevent casting the Hybrid's Base list spells unless the target's other realm is also negated.

Curses are not affected by regular dispelling. See Spell Law Section 10.2 for dealing with curses.

FLUID ELEMENTS.notes:
Note : See Spell Law Section 10.20 for additional details on Wall spells.

All vacuums created by the spells on this list also create a loud noise. The larger the radius the louder the noise. The GM may wish to rule that all within the radius must make a second RR or be deafened for 1 round per 10 failure (RR attack level equals the radius of the vacuum).

A Vacuum thrown at a creature made of gas will result in a Slaying IV Critical on the creature.

GATE MASTERY.notes:
Note : When allowed to choose more than one option on summoning spells, the same option may be chosen more than once. For ex ample, with a Summons III , two options are available. This means that if both options are used for the same thing, then three first-level creatures could be summoned, or one third-level creature could be summoned, or one first-level creature could be summoned for four times as long.

Because of the extremely strong and intimate bond created between caster and familiar, any attempt to dispel this bond suffers a penalty of 100 (normally a +100 bonus to the bond's RR against the dispelling attempt).

INVISIBLE WAYS.notes: Note : Only objects totally contained in the radius at the time of casting become invisible. Any object in the radius is under the restrictions given in Unseen I . See Spell Law Section 10.11 for more notes on the spells on this list.

LIVING CHANGE.notes:
Note : Unless otherwise stated, no change is made except to the living target of the spell, excluding items worn or carried, with the sole exception of any prosthetics added by the Lay Healer Base list Prosthetics.

A Size changing spell may be combined with a Change spell to take on a different form at a different Size.

A change in Size category carries with it all the normal advantages and disadvantages of the new Size. For example, for a Medium creature Enlarged to Big, increase their hits by 50%.

See Spell Law Section 10.21 for a discussion of spells with 'Kind' in their name.

LOFTY BRIDGE.notes:
Note : It should be clear from the spell descriptions, but experience with other game systems may lead to incorrect assumptions, so it should be noted that it is not possible for teleport error to place one inside a solid (or liquid, unless one has intended to teleport into a liquid environment) object. The spell would then fail and the teleporting individual(s) suffer stun (-50) as explained in the description of Long Door I [if the arrival point coincides with solid material, the target does not move, instead being stunned (-50) 1-10 rounds, and the PP for the spell are expended].

Spells that involve teleportation are normally quite noisy and difficult to silence. Air is being pushed about in a manner not unlike a thunderclap. Amount of noise depends on the size of the object teleported.

See Spell Law Section 10.15 for weight limits for movement spells.

LUMINOUS ELEMENTS.notes:
Note : See Spell Law Section 10.20 for additional details on Wall spells.

Consult Core Law Section 15.7 for dealing with light and darkness.

SHIELD MASTERY.notes: Note : When casting the Bladeturn / Deflections / Aim Untrue spells, the caster can concentrate in order to hold the spell until it can be applied to the allowed number of targets (See 'Delaying a Spell' in Spell Law Section 4.8 ).

SOLID ELEMENTS.notes: Note : See Spell Law Section 10.20 for additional details on Wall spells.

SPIRIT MASTERY.notes:
Note : The task required by a Quest may be extremely difficult, but it must at least appear to be possible. A Quest must be removed as a curse or mental illness; see Spell Law Section 10.2 for details.

See Spell Law Section 10.21 for a discussion of spells with 'Kind' in their name.

CONTROLLING SONGS.notes:
Note : Area of Effect and Duration are treated unusually and there are other special rules for this list. See Spell Law Section 10.1 .

An 'aggressive' action is defined as any action with the intent to directly harm any individual(s). Actions that result in harm indirectly to individuals are not 'aggressive'. Pulling the lever on the wall to drop an individual into a pit is an aggressive action (the action directly resulted in the harm). Running away to get help is not an aggressive action.

ENTERTAINING WAYS.notes: Note : Spells that involve teleportation are normally quite noisy and difficult to silence. Air is being pushed about in a manner not unlike a thunderclap. Amount of noise depends on the size of the object teleported. The spells on this list will muffle the sound and give it a 'theatrical' tone. but it will be clearly audible.

INSPIRING SONGS.notes: Note : Area of Effect and Duration are treated unusually. See Spell Law Section 10.1 .

ITEM LORE.notes: Note : See Spell Law Section 10.4 for more about detection spells.

SOUND CONTROL.notes: Note : See Spell Law Section 10.17 for details on using elemental spells, like Sphere of Silence and Quiet , on living targets.

CONCEALMENT MASTERY.notes:
Note : Illusions are one of the more complex and subtle types of magic and they are explained at length in Spell Law Section 10.10 .

For more information on invisibility, see Spell Law Section 10.11 .

MOVEMENT MASTERY.notes: Note : See Spell Law Section 10.15 for restrictions on encumbrance relating to movement spells.

SENSES.notes: Note : See Core Law Section 15.7 for more on vision in low light and darkness.

SMOKE AND MIRRORS.notes: Note : Illusions are one of the more complex and subtle types of magic and they are explained at length in Spell Law Section 10.10 .

TRADE MASTERY.notes: Note : For the purposes of this list, a machine is any deliberately constructed device with at least one moving part built to perform a specific function.

GUISES.notes: Note : Illusions are one of the more complex and subtle types of magic and they are explained at length in Spell Law Section 10.10 .

ILLUSION MASTERY.notes:
Note : If more than one option can be added to the Illusion or Phantasms spell, the same option can be chosen more than once. For Example - with an Illusion III , two options are available. The range could be doubled once to 200' and then doubled again to 400'.

Illusions are one of the more complex and subtle types of magic and they are explained at length in Spell Law Section 10.10 .

LIGHT MOLDING.notes:
Note : Illusions are one of the more complex and subtle types of magic and they are explained at length in Spell Law Section 10.10 .

Certain spells on this list have a radius effect that can be cast upon mobile targets (e.g., Light Control , Light , Utterlight , Utterdark ). See Spell Law Section 10.17 for more.

Consult Core Law Section 15.7 for dealing with light and darkness.

MIND SENSE MOLDING.notes:
Note : See Spell Law Section 10.4 for more about detection spells.

See Spell Law Section 10.21 for a discussion of spells with 'Kind' in their name.

SENSE MOLDING.notes: Note : Illusions are one of the more complex and subtle types of magic and they are explained at length in Spell Law Section 10.10 .

SOUND MOLDING.notes:
Note : Certain spells on this list have a radius effect that can be cast upon mobile targets (e.g., Sphere of Silence ). See Spell Law Section 10.17 for more.

Illusions are one of the more complex and subtle types of magic and they are explained at length in Spell Law Section 10.10 .

EARTH LAW.notes: Note : See Spell Law Section 10.20 for additional details on Wall spells.

FIRE LAW.notes: Note : See Spell Law Section 10.20 for additional details on Wall spells.

ICE LAW.notes: Note : See Spell Law Section 10.20 for additional details on Wall spells.

LIGHT LAW.notes:
Note : Certain spells on this list have a radius effect that can be cast upon mobile targets (e.g., Light , Darkness, Utterlight , Utterdark ). See Spell Law Section 10.17 for more.

Consult Core Law Section 15.7 for dealing with light and darkness.

WATER LAW.notes: Note : See Spell Law Section 10.20 for additional details on Wall spells.

WIND LAW.notes:
Note : See Spell Law Section 10.20 for additional details on Wall spells.

All vacuums created by the spells on this list also create a loud noise. The larger the radius the louder the noise. The GM may wish to rule that all within the radius must make a second RR or be deafened for 1 round per 10 failure (RR attack level equals the radius of the vacuum).

An elemental creature made of gas will be reduced to 1 AP per round if successfully attacked with an Air Stop spell (the creature must fit into the area of effect). A Vacuum thrown at a creature made of gas will result in a Slaying IV Critical on the creature.

DARKNESS.notes:
Note : Certain spells on this list have a radius effect that can be cast upon mobile targets (e.g., Darkness, Utterdark ). See Spell Law Section 10.17 for more.

Consult Core Law Section 15.7 for dealing with light and darkness.

DARK SUMMONS.notes:
Note : When allowed to choose more than one option on summoning spells, the same option may be chosen more than once. For example, with a Summons III , two options are available. This means that if both options are used for the same thing, then three first-level creatures could be summoned, or one third-level creature could be summoned, or one first-level creature could be summoned for four times as long.

Because of the extremely strong and intimate bond created between caster and familiar, any attempt to dispel this bond suffers a penalty of 100 (normally a +100 bonus to the bond's RR against the dispelling attempt). Investitures have only a bias of 50 in their favor, but must be undone one by one, starting from the highest level Investiture down to the last. Only once all Investiture spells are dispelled may the Familiar bond be subject to dispelling.

FOUL TRANSFORMATIONS.notes: Note : The exact form of these transformations will vary from caster to caster, but they will always be more or less horrific.

NECROMANCY MASTERY.notes:
Note : Casting a Control Undead or Command Undead spell successfully (i.e., it is not resisted) will not turn the target hostile after the period of control is over.

The Control spells (but not Command spells) on this list will also work on the mindless undead.

Liches of all types must be created by passing directly to undeath from life, without going through the process of dying and cannot be created by means of this list. Individual GMs may choose to exclude certain other kinds of undead from this form of origin.

See Creature Law for more information on undead.

NECROMANTIC WAYS.notes:
Note : Mindless undead are any undead that have the Mindless flaw.

Normally undead created by this list are Standard Created Undead, but other forms of mindless undead may be created with a suitable corpse (or spirit) and a successful Spell Mastery maneuver of Medium difficulty at a penalty of -10 per Class of the undead to be created. If this maneuver fails, the corpse turns to dust or the spirit vanishes beyond recall.

See Creature Law for more information on undead.

BRILLIANCE.notes:
Note : None of the 'Aura' spells ( Aura , True Aura , Mass Aura , and Alkar ) are cumulative with each other or Blur . The Gamemaster may wish to allow the bonus from these spells to apply to Leadership as well as defense.

Certain spells on this list have a radius effect that can be cast upon mobile targets (e.g., Light , Darkness , Utterlight , Utterdark ). See Section 10.17 for more.

Consult Core Law Section 15.7 for dealing with light and dark ness.

CLOAKING.notes:
Note : Cloaking spells are not Invisibility spells and none of the normal rules for invisibility apply (e.g., the caster does not become 'visible' when he attacks or is hit, etc.).

Illusions (such as Façade , Camouflage , and Shadow Mentalist ) are one of the more complex and subtle types of magic and they are explained at length in Spell Law Section 10.10 . Cloaking is a form of 'mind trick' and is discussed in that same section.

DAMAGE RESISTANCE.notes: Note : When under the effects of an Unpain spell, there are no pen alties for hits lost. Full effects of the lost hits occur when the spell duration ends. However, if the hits are healed before the duration ends, there is no effect. So, a character could be reduced to -38 hits while sustained by Unpain , but restored to 2 hits before the duration of the spell ended. He would never pass out. Likewise, if Unpain allows fighting beyond lethal hit loss, this has no effect until the spell expires.

DELVING.notes: Note : See Spell Law Section 10.4 for more about detection spells.

DETECTIONS.notes: Note : See Spell Law Section 10.4 for more about detection spells.

SEEMINGS.notes: Note : For a full explanation of the operations of overlays and seemings, see Spell Law Section 10.10 .

SELF HEALING.notes:
Note : The wound healing spells on this list will treat all types of wounds except nerve and brain damage.

See Spell Law Section 10.9 for the application of wound-healing spells (various Relief , Healing , and Healing True spells). While medical treatment of the wound is miraculously immediate, the body will still need a period of recovery before the injury has healed, depending on several factors, including which type of wound-healing spell is used.

SPELL RESISTANCE.notes: Note : A Hybrid spell will be affected by a Cancel or Shield spell that is effective against either of its hybridized realms.

ATTACK AVOIDANCE.notes: Note : When casting the Bladeturn / Deflections / Aim Untrue spells, the caster can concentrate in order to hold the spell until it can be applied to the allowed number of targets (See 'Delaying a Spell' in Section 4.8).

GAS MANIPULATION.notes:
Note : All vacuums created by the spells on this list also create a loud noise. The larger the radius the louder the noise. The GM may wish to rule that all within the radius must make a second RR or be deafened for 1 round per 10 failure (RR attack level equals the radius of the vacuum).

An elemental creature made of gas will be reduced to 1 AP per round if successfully attacked with an Air Stop spell (the creature must fit into the area of effect). A Vacuum thrown at a creature made of gas will result in a Slaying IV Critical on the creature. A Whirling Winds has no effect on an elemental creature made of gas, though creatures shape-changed into gas are affected normally.

MIND'S DOOR.notes:
Note : It should be clear from the spell descriptions, but experience with other game systems may lead to incorrect assumptions, so it should be noted that it is not possible for teleport error to place one inside a solid (or liquid, unless one has intended to teleport into a liquid environment) object. The spell would then fail and the teleporting individual(s) suffer stun (-50) as explained in the description of Minor Long Door [if the arrival point coincides with solid material, the caster does not move, instead being stunned (-50) 1-10 rounds, and the PP for the spell are still expended].

Spells that involve teleportation are normally quite noisy and difficult to silence. Air is being pushed about in a manner not unlike a thunderclap. Amount of noise depends on the size of the object teleported.

MIND MASTERY.notes:
Note : The 'Presence' ability detects minds of better than animal intelligence (i.e., creatures with the 'Animalistic' or 'Mindless' flaws are not detected). The caster will be aware of proximity to within 10' distance, and a 1 AP action will provide general direction (above, below, left, right, before, or behind) to one mind. If a detected mind belongs to a seen and recognized (as intelligent) being, then the caster will be able to identify the detected mind as belonging to that being.

See Spell Law Section 10.21 for a discussion of spells with 'Kind' in their name.

MOVEMENT.notes: Note : See Spell Law Section 10.15 on weight limits for spells.

SENSE MASTERY.notes:
Note : See Spell Law Section 10.4 for more about detection spells.

See Core Law Section 15.7 for more on vision in low light and darkness.

SHIFTING.notes: Note : See Spell Law Section 10.21 for a discussion of spells with 'Kind' in their name.

BLOOD MASTERY.notes:
Note : A flesh wound is also classified as a 'skin & tissue injury'. Injury penalties from cuts (i.e., wounds that also caused bleeding) are likewise flesh wounds and 'skin & tissue injuries,' and are treated with Flesh Relief or Flesh Healing spells.

See Core Law Section 13.1 .

See Spell Law Section 10.9 for the application of wound-healing spells (various Relief , Healing , and Healing True spells). While medical treatment of the wound is miraculously immediate, the body will still need a period of recovery before the injury has healed, depending on several factors, including which type of wound-healing spell is used.

In no case do these spells allow the disease or poison removed to make an RR.

Parasitic infestation is considered a disease for purposes of this list.

BONE MASTERY.notes: Note : See Spell Law Section 10.9 for the application of wound-healing spells (various Relief , Healing , and Healing True spells). While medical treatment of the wound is miraculously immediate, the body will still need a period of recovery before the injury has healed, depending on several factors, including which type of wound-healing spell is used.

CONCUSSION MASTERY.notes: Note : See Spell Law Section 10.9 for the application of wound-healing spells (various Relief , Healing , and Healing True spells). While medical treatment of the wound is miraculously immediate, the body will still need a period of recovery before the injury has healed, depending on several factors, including which type of wound-healing spell is used.

MUSCLE MASTERY.notes: Note : See Spell Law Section 10.9 for the application of wound-healing spells (various Relief , Healing , and Healing True spells). While medical treatment of the wound is miraculously immediate, the body will still need a period of recovery before the injury has healed, depending on several factors, including which type of wound-healing spell is used.

NERVE AND ORGAN MASTERY.notes: Note : See Spell Law Section 10.9 for the application of wound-healing spells (various Relief , Healing , and Healing True spells). While medical treatment of the wound is miraculously immediate, the body will still need a period of recovery before the injury has healed, depending on several factors, including which type of wound-healing spell is used.

PROSTHETICS.notes:
Note : Any attempts to dispel an Animation spell are done at a -50 penalty.

As used here, a 'prosthetic' is an artificial body part formed and (potentially) animated by magic. This usage is distinct from real world artificial limbs, properly called 'protheses' (sing., 'prothesis'), the art of their creation being 'prosthetics'. In mixed science and magic settings, Lay-Healer-created prosthetics and technological protheses may both be in use.

ASSASSINATION MASTERY.notes: Note : Illusions (such as Concealed Object ) are one of the more complex and subtle types of magic and they are explained at length in Spell Law Section 10.10 .

DISGUISE MASTERY.notes:
Note : Illusions (such as Glamour and Façade spells) are one of the more complex and subtle types of magic and they are explained at length in Spell Law Section 10.10 .

See Spell Law Section 10.21 for a discussion of spells with 'Kind' in their name.

ESCAPES.notes: Note : Spells that involve teleportation are normally quite noisy and difficult to silence. The Magent's 'Silenced' versions are much quieter, producing only a soft 'pop' that would normally go unnoticed except in an absolutely still environment. Of course, being seen using these spells by anyone but one's own associates is basically the equivalent of wearing a tunic embroidered with the words 'I AM AN ASSASSIN. KILL ME NOW.'

MISDIRECTIONS.notes: Note : The Eyewitness spells create a specialized Overlay, as detailed in Spell Law Section 10.10 .

POISON MASTERY.notes:
Note : Any spell on this list that requires the caster to touch a poison automatically gives the caster immunity to the effects of the poison for the duration of the spell.

Some Gamemasters may wish to allow this list to affect narcotics as well as poisons in the traditional sense. In this case, a Spell Mastery roll should be required, at a Medium difficulty.

MIND CONTROL.notes:
Note : The task required by a Geas may be extremely difficult, but it must at least appear to be possible. A Geas must be removed as a curse or mental illness; see Spell Law Section 10.2 for details.

See Spell Law Section 10.21 for a discussion of spells with 'Kind' in their name.

MIND SPEECH.notes: Notes : Except where communication is noted as being 'one-way', the spells below create a 'two-way' communication between the target and the caster. The caster is not required to speak aloud. The target speaks aloud, but the caster is actually reading the surface thoughts of the target (some targets may learn to use mental communication - any caster who knows this list is presumed to have this ability). This will allow simple communication of physical ideas across language barriers (things where the word-meaning can be associated with visual images), but cannot handle more abstract ideas without a shared language.

PRESENCE.notes: Note : The 'Presence' ability detects minds of better than animal intelligence (i.e., creatures with the 'Animalistic' or 'Mindless' flaws are not detected). The caster will be aware of proximity to within 10' distance, and a 1 AP action will provide general direction (above, below, left, right, before, or behind) to one mind. If a detected mind belongs to a seen and recognized (as intelligent) being, then the caster will be able to identify the detected mind as belonging to that being.

SENSE CONTROL.notes: Notes : All of the sensations created by spells on this list are strictly mental (i.e., not real). For example - the sounds created with Audio Attack are heard only in the target's head and will work even on a deaf person.

BODY REINS.notes: Note : When under the effects of an Unpain spell, there are no penalties for hits lost beyond 25%. Full effects of the lost hits occur when the spell duration ends. However, if the hits are healed before the duration ends, there is no effect. So, a character could be reduced to -38 hits while sustained by Unpain , but restored to 2 hits before the duration of the spell ended. He would never pass out. Likewise, if Unpain allows fighting beyond lethal hit loss, this has no effect until the spell expires.

COMBAT MASTERY.notes: Note : All Strike spells on this list are only effective against an opponent who has been 'studied' using Study Opponent .

MONK'S BRIDGE.notes: Note : Spells that involve teleportation are normally quite noisy and difficult to silence. Air is being pushed about in a manner not unlike a thunderclap. Amount of noise depends on the size of the object teleported.

MONK'S SENSE.notes:
Note : See Spell Law Section 10.4 for more about detection spells.

See Core Law Section 15.7 for more on vision in low light and darkness.

MIND DEATH.notes:
Note : When a target loses experience points, this has nothing to do with experience levels. The lost experience points simply means that the character will have to gain that many more before rising to the next level.

The spells on this list may be reversed by healing the brain.

MIND DISEASE.notes:
Note : When selecting a subject for the target's Neurosis , Phobia , Psychosis , etc, the caster cannot choose something the target is in constant contact with (e.g., air, dirt, the Essence, etc.).

Mental diseases caused by the spells on this list are curses with mental effects. See Spell Law Section 10.2 for treatment.

MIND EROSION.notes: Note : Spells on this list cannot reduce a stat bonus below -15. Spells on this list may be reversed by healing the brain.

MIND ILLUSIONS.notes: Note : Many of these spells affect a target's perception of a situation. The duration of the spell is how long the target will incorrectly perceive the situation. At the end of the duration, if the situation has ended, the target will remember the situation incorrectly (as that was how he perceived it).

MIND SUBVERSION.notes: Note : The spells on this list should be treated as curses with mental effects. See Spell Law Section 10.2 for treatment.

BLOOD WAYS.notes:
Note : A flesh wound is also classified as a 'skin & tissue injury'. Injury penalties from cuts (i.e., wounds that also caused bleeding) are likewise flesh wounds and 'skin & tissue injuries,' and are treated with Flesh Relief or Flesh Healing spells.

See Core Law Section 13.1 .

See Spell Law Section 10.9 for the application of wound-healing spells (various Relief , Healing , and Healing True spells). While medical treatment of the wound is miraculously immediate, the body will still need a period of recovery before the injury has healed, depending on several factors, including which type of wound-healing spell is used.

BONE WAYS.notes: Note : See Spell Law Section 10.9 for the application of wound-healing spells (various Relief , Healing , and Healing True spells). While medical treatment of the wound is miraculously immediate, the body will still need a period of recovery before the injury has healed, depending on several factors, including which type of wound-healing spell is used.

MUSCLE WAYS.notes: Note : See Spell Law Section 10.9 for the application of wound-healing spells (various Relief , Healing , and Healing True spells). While medical treatment of the wound is miraculously immediate, the body will still need a period of recovery before the injury has healed, depending on several factors, including which type of wound-healing spell is used.

ORGAN WAYS.notes: Note : See Spell Law Section 10.9 for the application of wound-healing spells (various Relief , Healing , and Healing True spells). While medical treatment of the wound is miraculously immediate, the body will still need a period of recovery before the injury has healed, depending on several factors, including which type of wound-healing spell is used.

SURFACE WAYS.notes: Note : See Spell Law Section 10.9 for the application of wound-healing spells (various Relief , Healing , and Healing True spells). While medical treatment of the wound is miraculously immediate, the body will still need a period of recovery before the injury has healed, depending on several factors, including which type of wound-healing spell is used.

GAS ALTERATION.notes:
Note : All vacuums created by the spells on this list also create a loud noise. The larger the radius the louder the noise. The GM may wish to rule that all within the radius must make a second RR or be deafened for 1 round per 10 failure (RR attack level equals the radius of the vacuum).

An elemental creature made of gas will be reduced to 1 AP per round if successfully attacked with an Air Stop spell (the creature must fit into the area of effect). A Vacuum thrown at a creature made of gas will result in a Slaying IV Critical on the creature. A Whirling Winds has no effect on an elemental creature made of gas, though creatures shape-changed into gas are affected normally.

HIDING.notes: Note : For guidelines on handling invisibility, see Spell Law Section 10.11 .

MYSTICAL CHANGE.notes: Note : See Spell Law Section 10.21 for a discussion of spells with 'Kind' in their name.

FLESH DESTRUCTION.notes: Note : For non-humanoid targets, the GM may need to use some judgment regarding 'limb' spells. A Limb Pain spell that affects a wing would prevent flight, for example.

GAS DESTRUCTION.notes:
Note : All vacuums created by the spells on this list also create a loud noise. The larger the radius the louder the noise. The GM may wish to rule that all within the radius must make a second RR or be deafened for 1 round per 10 failure (RR attack level equals the radius of the vacuum).

An elemental creature made of gas will be reduced to 1 AP per round if successfully attacked with an Air Stop spell (the creature must fit into the area of effect). A Vacuum thrown at a creature made of gas will result in a Slaying IV Critical on the creature.

When the oxygen in an area falls below 50% of normal, anyone in that area must make an RR (attack level is 1) or fall asleep (this RR is modified by -2 for every 1% under 50%). Of course, if the % drops below 10%, suffocation becomes a danger. All fire spells in an area of low oxygen are modified by -2 (or 2% effectiveness for non-attack spells) for every 1% under 50% of normal oxygen.

MIND DESTRUCTION.notes:
Note : When a target loses experience points, this has nothing to do with experience levels. The lost experience points simply means that the character will have to gain that many more before rising to the next level. The experience loss may be reversed by healing the brain.

Initiative penalties from Disorientation , Unbalance , and Falter are not cumulative.

SOUL DESTRUCTION.notes: Note : Neurosis , Guilt , Paranoia , Unsoul Curse and Chronic Panic are curses, with mental effects. See Spell Law Section 10.2 for treatment options. Absolution does not kill the body, so Dark Absolution leaves a living, but soulless body.

STARLORE.notes: When using this list, the GM or the player working with the GM should determine a set of 10-20 celestial features which constitute the influences as understood by the character's faith. These may be planets or other celestial bodies, deities, mythological creatures, constellations, elements, etc. All spells referring to “influences” will reference these celestial features. See the notes preceding these spell lists for more information.

FAR VISIONS.notes: Spells which project senses (e.g., Observe, Long Ear) cannot be combined with other sense-enhancing spells. For example, Observe and Stonesight cannot be combined in order to see through stone at a distant location.

VISION GUARD.notes: If the caster of an information spell (e.g., Scrying, Detect, Divination ) suspects their efforts are being interfered with, they may make a RR at -50 (-20 for Seers and Astrologers). If successful, they are aware that magical interference is present. A Spell Lore maneuver may determine the nature of that interference. The caster of the information spell may choose to attempt to pierce that interference, in which case the interfering spell (e.g. Cloud Scrying ) must make a RR (at +0 if the diviner is a Seer, +10 if an Astrologer, and +20 otherwise); if it fails, the protection is pierced and nullified.

WAY OF THE VOICE.notes: An “aggressive” action is defined as any action with the intent to directly harm any individual(s). Actions that result in harm indirectly to individuals are not “aggressive”. Pulling the lever on the wall to drop an individual into a pit is an aggressive action (the action directly resulted in the harm). Running away to get help is not an aggressive action.

MIND VISIONS.notes: The “Presence” ability detects minds of better than animal intelligence (i.e., creatures with the “Animalistic” or “Mindless” flaws are not detected). The caster will be aware of proximity to within 10' distance, and a 1 AP action will provide general direction (above, below, left, right, before, or behind) to one mind. If a detected mind belongs to a seen and recognized (as intelligent) being, then the caster will be able to identify the detected mind as belonging to that being.

STARTLIGHTS.notes: None of the Self Aura spells are cumulative with each other or with Blur or other Aura spells.

DEMONIC BINDING.notes:
Note : Talents, spell lists, and skills manifest randomly from those the embedded entity possesses. However, talents will be chosen from among those between the DP limit of the Manifest Talent spell used and the limit of the next lower Manifest Talent spell, whenever possible, giving some control.

The GM may determine that any given talent is unsuitable for placement in an item or may place certain restrictions on it, as not all of the many creature talents may be suitable as item powers in a given setting.

In addition to demons, spells on this list may be used on other types of Extra Planar creatures as defined in Creature Law , including to bind them into items.

GENERAL ENCHANTMENT.notes:
Note : The skill bonus from a General spell may be applied to all specializations of a specialized skill by doubling the time cost in days. All skills within a single skill category can receive the bonus by quadrupling the time.

The time and PP cost of the General spell may be reduced to half normal by restricting the applicability of the bonus (e.g., RRs vs only poisons or only Evil Channeling). By default, the RR bonus applies to the item itself and to the wearer/wielder/bearer as well. Reducing the bonus by 5 allows extending the bonus to a 5' radius effect. The radius may be increased by 5' for each further reduction of the bonus by 5. Thus a General V spell could produce a +25 bonus against Essence for the item and its user, a +20 bonus in a 5' radius, a +15 bonus in a 10' radius, a +10 bonus in a 15' radius, or a +5 bonus in a 20' radius.

The GM is the final arbitrator as to what skills a General enchantment can provide a bonus to for any given item. GMs may wish to limit such enchantments to those skills that relate to the item's normal use. Disallowed skill/item combinations may still be achieved through use of the Sanctifier's Sacred Skill spells, and similar enchantments are possible through the Psychographer's lists. The market value of such items will generally assume General enchantment, even when this is not the case.

DEEP IMPRESSIONS.notes:
Note : Items animated through Remote Operation , Station Keeping or Remote Mission abilities may come under attack, especially weapons. The item will have an AT (10 for hard metal items like swords) and a DB (use the wielder's Quickness bonus, although an item with a Quickness bonus can use that instead, and add any bonus for material). If successfully attacked, many results should be ignored: stuns, bleeding, etc. An attack that knocks the target down immediately defeats the item and it loses its animation. Otherwise, the item can absorb 5 hits per level of the item before deanimating. Breakage results from criticals are applied to the item, and the item will suffer normally.

The Spell Storage capability is an independent function. Unlike a Spell Store spell, its use does not interfere with the spell-casting abilities of the wielder or the item.

SACRED STRUCTURES.notes: Note : The features of sacred ground as such are dependent on the setting and possibly the religion/deity to which the sacred ground is dedicated. However, this note defines the default values and the GM may work from there to make whatever adjustments are required by the setting. Firstly, there are several spell failure results in Channeling that can require time on sacred ground for recovery. Secondly, those entering sacred ground with hostile intent are discomforted; if an attempt is made to carry out hostile intent, the individual in question must make a Fear check (although only against a level 1 fear source, so powerful and/or determined enemies will probably succeed). Evil magic suffers a -10 to SCRs. Reverse this to +10 SCRs for evil magic if the site is 'unholy'. Other variations are possible: a war god's sacred ground may hamper calm, charm, and other peace-making spells and aid strife-fomenting spells, while the sacred ground of a fire god may aid fire and hamper cold and ice.

WEAPON ENCHANTMENT.notes:
Note : Weapon and Slaying spells can be applied to items that cast spells using the Directed Spells skill at double the time cost (e.g., Weapon II can be used to give a Wand of Shock Bolts a +10 OB, but adds 16 days to the creation time instead of the usual 8).

Slaying applies to a single creature Variety (e.g., bears, skullbeasts) or a single profession or Evil spellcasters by default. By tripling the days spent for this spell, it can apply to a creature Type (e.g., carnivores, corporeal undead) or to Pure Spellcasters of a given Realm, Semi Spellcasters of a given Realm, Hybrid Spellcasters, or Arms Professions. For five times the normal time requirement, it can apply to an entire creature Category (e.g., animals, undead). Time required can be reduced to half by applying to a select sub group (female Titans, spell-casting Trolls, Evil elves, etc.) The subgroup should not be more than about half the population.

For Weapon spells used to create an additional bonus, the bonus applies to a Type (e.g., reptiles, demons) by default. Cut the time cost in half if it applies only to a Variety (e.g., alligators, corvox); double the time if it applies to a Category (e.g., animals, extra planar creatures). Use the same equivalents for profession types as for Slaying .

Vampiric Effects : The Vampiric Weapon spell can bestow one of the following properties. Multiple Vampiric Weapon spells can provide multiple properties. Weapon causes Life Drain imposing a -1 Co penalty per severity of the critical (e.g., a C critical imposes a -3 penalty). RR versus Essence applies unless this ability is added twice (as one power with doubled time costs). Weapon can heal the wielder of minor injuries and weariness. For every concussion hit that the weapon inflicts, the wielder may recover 1 concussion hit or remove -1 in fatigue penalties. Weapon can drain Power Points from those it harms and transfer them to the wielder or to itself. The weapon drains 3 PP per severity of the critical (e.g., 3 PP for an A crit or 12 PP for a D crit). These PP then are added to the weapon or its wielder to the limit of normal maximum PP. RR versus Essence applies unless this ability is added twice. Weapon feeds on the souls of those it kills. When it delivers a lethal blow, once the foe is dead, the weapon absorbs some of the life energy of the soul. For each level of the slain, a concussion hit can be recovered by the wielder, a -1 penalty due to breakage on the weapon may be repaired, or 1 PP may be recovered by the weapon or its wielder. This ability may be increased by adding it multiple times to a maximum of five times (for 5 hits, -5 breakage recovery, or 5 PP per level of slain), at which point it acts as a Dark Absolution , destroying the soul of the slain. Weapon can convert hits of damage done to power. For every three concussion hits of damage delivered, the weapon or its wielder may recover 1 PP (up to normal maximum). Weapon enhances bleeding. For any result of bleeding X hits/ round, this is increased to X+1 hits/round. This ability may be added multiple times for increased effect.

DISENCHANTMENTS.notes:
Note : The core rule is to roll a single RR for all items in an individual's aura (though items with a higher level than their bearer may still resist while others succumb), except in the case of Disenchantment True . If magical items are not too plentiful, a GM may wish to give each item its own RR in all cases.

Items empowered by the caster's own faith (i.e., works of a Sanctifier of the same religion or gifts from his god) are immune to all effects of this list.

Autonomous 'items' (i.e., any enchanted item that functions without a 'user' - golems, magical traps and machines, Symbols, etc.) resist at twice their level.

Enchanted locations are not affected by this list at all.

DIVINE TOUCH.notes:
Note : The use of these spells does not require a Work or Make spell, instead requiring merely the Consecration spell (Sacred Purpose list), but the item to be enchanted must meet the requirements of association with the religion of the caster and any requirements of the religion for materials, ritual purification, or other standards (e.g., the God of Justice might reject an item that incorporates a 'blood diamond'). Furthermore, the GM must limit what abilities may be allowed for a given religion. This list is quite powerful, with narrowness of scope as the primary balancing tool. When in doubt, rule it out. Only those abilities and objects with a clear mythological or theological link to the caster's power source should be allowed.

While Sacred Spell combines the effects of the Adept's Embed and Daily spells, the spell to be embedded is still required to be cast each day of the enchantment process and does add to the required working days and PP. Also note that this process does not have the flexibility of the Adept's process. A spell can only be made to be cast once per day.

MAGICAL WEAVES.notes: Note : Normal flight piloting a flying carpet is as simple as walking, but in a tactical situation, in difficult weather, or under any other circumstances where the carpet will be doing more than continuing in a straight line, hovering, or making a gentle, predictable movement, the controller will need to Concentrate in order to make the necessary adjustments to the carpet's flight.

GOLEM MAKING.notes: Note : See Treasure Law Section 5.4 for details on the creation and management of golems.

SPIRIT BINDING.notes:
Note : Talents, spell lists, and skills manifest randomly from those the embedded entity possesses. However, talents will be chosen from among those between the DP limit of the Manifest Talent spell used and the limit of the next lower Manifest Talent spell, whenever possible, giving some control.

The GM may determine that any given talent is unsuitable for placement in an item or may place certain restrictions on it, as not all of the many creature talents may be suitable as item powers in a given setting.

CREATURE CULTIVATION.notes: Note: See Treasure Law Section 5.5 for details on the creation and management of cultivated creatures.

SACRED LAND.notes:
Note : The features of sacred ground as such are dependent on the setting and possibly the religion/deity to which the sacred ground is dedicated. However, this note defines the default values and the GM may work from there to make whatever adjustments are required by the setting. Firstly, there are several spell failure results in Channeling that can require time on sacred ground for recovery. Secondly, those entering sacred ground with hostile intent are discomforted; if an attempt is made to carry out hostile intent, the individual in question must make a Fear check (although only against a level 1 fear source unless otherwise specified by a particular spell, so powerful and/or determined enemies will probably succeed). Evil magic suffers a -10 to SCRs. Reverse this to +10 SCRs for evil magic if the site is 'unholy'.

Other variations are possible: a war god's sacred ground may hamper calm, charm, and other peace-making spells and aid strife-fomenting spells, while the sacred ground of a fire god may aid fire and hamper cold and ice. When the site is free-standing, like a lone standing stone or a sacred tree, the effects of the site enchantments will cover an area within a 1 yard radius (beyond the radius of the site itself) per level of the site.

STANDING CHANNELS.notes: A Standing Channel is a spell that has been given a Permanent duration by being bound to an object called a Focus. By default, the Focus is located at the Standing Channel 's focal point, the place where the caster of the spell is considered to be for purposes of locating the spell effect (e.g., a spell with a range of Touch can only take effect on a target in contact with the focal point, while a spell with a radius of 50' and range of Self will radiate out 50' from the focal point, and a spell with a range of 100' may have its effects located anywhere within 100' of the focal point). Offset Focus spells allow the Focus to be moved some distance away from the focal point. If the Focus is ever moved beyond that distance, the Standing Channel is dispelled. If the Focus is destroyed or broken, the Standing Channel will also be dispelled. If the Standing Channel is dispelled normally, but the Focus is left in place (or at least intact and within range of the focal point), then the Standing Channel will regenerate itself one day after being dispelled.

MOOD IMPRESSIONS.notes: Note : The effects of this list require more GM judgment than most to adjudicate. For this reason, some GMs may wish to not include this list in their worlds. The effects can be both subtle and powerful, with any mood being something of a double-edged sword. Possible moods may include calm, happiness, harmony, friendliness, optimism, pessimism, discord, hatefulness, fear, anxiety, anger, grief, awe, despair, hope, rationality, doubt, certainty, nostalgia, curiosity, lust, revulsion, weariness, perkiness, excitement, and apathy. Certainly, other moods are possible and some of those suggested might be undesirable in a given game. It is the GM's call as to whether any given mood may be used or not. GMs who allow grammatical moods are to be saluted for creativity if they can make it work, but you are on your own.

SHOE ENCHANTMENTS.notes: Note : Regardless of spell name, all spells on this list apply to all forms of footwear: boots, shoes, slippers, sandals, etc.

POWER IMPRESSIONS.notes:
Note : Emplaced spells are available to be cast like embedded spells, but emplacement does not provide power for the spells. Thus no Make Wand , Daily , or similar spells need be employed in the item's creation, but when the spell is used the necessary PP must come from either the user or the item (e.g., from Implant Power ). The spell is then cast at the level of the user, unless the item is intelligent, in which case the item's level may be used instead. If the user provides the PP, the user must be of the right Realm, or the item must have the Adaptive Power ability.

The 'template' is a being that has the attribute to be implanted. If the template is not the caster, then the Template Link spell must be cast at the start of the enchantment process. Abilities not possessed by the template cannot be implanted (i.e., an Emplace List True does not allow emplacing spells above the level to which the template knows the list).

The GM may determine that any given talent is unsuitable for emplacement in an item or may place certain restrictions on it, as not all of the many creature talents may be suitable as item powers in a given setting.

ENCHANTMENT MASTERY.notes:
Note : Normally the abilities granted by spells on this list apply to a particular realm or to a particular Hybrid profession. An item that works for a single non-Hybrid profession halves the number of working days and the PP for the enchantment (e.g., a +3 Bard Spell Adder will only take 7 working days and 7 PP for the Spell Adder III spell). An item (excludes PP Multipliers) that applies only to a single list takes one tenth the time. An item that only works for Evil spellcasters takes one third. An item that works for two realms (including any Hybrid using those realms) takes double the time and PP. A Universal item (works for any realm) takes triple. Note that these time changes apply only to the spell(s) from this list affected by the non-standard scope, not any other enchantments on the same item. Note that Increase Power has its own defined cost reductions, which override this note when dealing with single spell lists, but may otherwise combine with the price alterations here.

All of the above items must be held in one hand by default. If the item is being employed in the casting of a spell, that hand is considered to be a 'free hand' for the purposes of Spell Law Table 4-2 . If the item is to function when merely worn or carried on one's person, double the required working time and PPs.

BLADERUNES.notes: Notes : Bladerunes may be applied only to weapons and shields. Indeed, in earlier eras, a less-developed form of this list could apply its special runes only to bladed weapons, which led to the name which these runes still bear. In order for a bladerune's effect to happen, the wielder of the item bearing the bladerune must activate it. This requires an instantaneous action and a successful Runes maneuver. Multiple bladerunes may be activated at once, with a separate maneuver for each. The Runes maneuver is penalized by the level of the spell used to create the bladerune (i.e., to activate a Weapon Rune V , the wielder must make a Runes maneuver with a -30 modifier to his roll). The Anchoring Rune is an exception; it is considered to be active whenever the bladerune that it is anchoring is active. When a bladerune 'fades' it disappears from the item, its magic spent. Because bladerunes are a superficial enchantment, rather than the deeply embedded magic of regular Alchemy, they are subject to dispelling like other spells. Also, the caster of a bladerune spell may cancel it like a normal spell, causing the bladerune to prematurely fade. They are still subject to spells from the Disenchantments list as well. A bladerune counts as an 'active spell' (e.g., it is detected by Detect Essence ). Bladerunes do not make an item count as magical in combat, except during a round in which the rune effect is active. They provide for an RR as noted below in Note G . Most items can be inscribed with a maximum of four bladerunes. Items made from inherently magical materials (e.g., Eog) can hold up to six bladerunes, while items of Starfall can hold up to eight. Once a bladerune has faded, it no longer counts against this maximum (being gone) and may be replaced with the same or another bladerune. Bladerune effects are not cumulative: the OBs of multiple Weapon Runes , the bonuses of Shield Runes , the RR mods of Resistance Runes , etc., may not be totaled. Only one of each type of bladerune may be effective at a time. However, bladerunes of different types may be utilized together; e.g., a wielder might in one round benefit from an OB addition, a Shield addition, an RR mod, and an additional critical. However, all Runes involved would be subject to their normal rules of 'fading'. Note that bladerunes are created by Force spells; a magical item must fail an RR in order for a bladerune to be placed on it. Intelligent items can control their own bladerunes unless the item is completely dominated by the wielder. Add 1 to the level of the item for purposes of this RR for each bladerune already present (note that a non-magical item must start making RRs for any bladerunes added after the first). Intelligent items may be 'willing targets' for a -50 RR modifier. This is not cumulative with Runic Surface .

SKIN ENCHANTMENT.notes:
Note : The 'tattoo' may actually be any form of permanent marking, whether genuine tattoos, branding, ritual scarring, or special treatments that permanently dye fur. Depending on the technique, some plucking/shearing may be required in order to reach a markable surface.

Each magical tattoo requires an amount of the body surface area available for tattooing. This is expressed as a percentage and the percentage used may never exceed 100%.

These tattoos create what are essentially innate powers, by enchanting the living target. They are powered by the tattoo-bearer's own aura. They also cause the tattooed to always be considered to radiate active Channeling magic for detection purposes.

ELEMENTAL BINDING.notes:
Note : Talents, spell lists, and skills manifest randomly from those the embedded entity possesses. However, talents will be chosen from among those between the DP limit of the Manifest Talent spell used and the limit of the next lower Manifest Talent spell, whenever possible, giving some control.

The GM may determine that any given talent is unsuitable for placement in an item or may place certain restrictions on it, as not all of the many creature talents may be suitable as item powers in a given setting.

SKILL IMPRESSIONS.notes:
Note : The skill bonuses implanted by the various Skill spells may be used in place of the item-wielder's own skill bonus; it does not add to the existing bonus. The bonus that is implanted is the bonus from skill ranks only and it replaces bonus from skill ranks only. This only affects skill bonus, not skill ranks. In order to get an effect of increased skill ranks (e.g., for passive dodging or Ambush), Rank Impression must be used. If the skill is specialized, the bonus will be for a single specialization.

The 'template' is a being that has the attribute to be implanted. If the template is not the caster, then the Template Link spell from the Power Impressions spell list must be cast at the start of the enchantment process.

CHARM CREATION.notes: Charms : This spell list allows for the creation of magical items which last until certain circumstances occur. They are made from an assortment of bits and pieces of mostly organic materials (feathers, hair, bits of bone, etc.) and frequently worn about the neck, though they may be carried anywhere on one's person while remaining effective. Normally, these charms are created for an individual and work only for that individual. Some token of that individual is included in the charm. A 'token' may be some part of that person: a bit of hair, a fingernail, or perhaps a drop of blood; it may also be a part of something with a long or close association with the person, such as a shred of a scarf worn for months or a ring gifted by a loved one. Because of this process, charms (including all spells from this list) are generally relatively cheap to make: 1 sp per day for materials, rather than 2 sp. Furthermore, if the user is to be the caster, the time requirement is halved. A charm can be made that anyone can use, but this requires stronger magic and the cost of materials is normal. Charms do not require Consecration or Make or Work spells.

SACRED PURPOSE.notes: Note : Blessed Weapon can be reversed to Unblessed Weapon to create a bonus against creatures of light. Holy Weapon can be reversed to Unholy Weapon , providing bonuses against Good entities (includes anyone Channeling power from a Good source, Champions, and various others according to setting). Slaying works on Champions, other non-Evil Extra Planar creatures, and non-Evil members of species classified as Races in Creature Law . Other variations may be possible in worlds with grand conflicts other than good versus evil. Purification is already Corruption from the point-of-view of victims.
